fix(ui): use the conversation font in the quote panel

## Linked issue

Refs #172

## Type of change

Fix (UI): the quote panel uses the conversation font.

## Reasoning

The host applies its own UI font to everything it renders, with a selector strong enough to override any font a plugin sets. Inside the quote dialog the quoted text therefore fell back to the system font stack, so bold looked regular on machines whose system font has no bold face and the dialog did not match the conversation.

## Goals

- Quoted text, headings, lists and inline code in the panel use the same font as the conversation and follow the Clear Chat font setting (embedded font by default, system font when chosen).

## Non-goals

- The sent text, the quotation bar, selection, expand/collapse and the test ids.

## Changes

- `client/components/quote-reply.tsx`: the quoted block opts out of the host font rule with the same helper the settings page and step details already use.
- `test/helpers/tool-harness.cjs`: the harness no longer stubs that helper, so the real one is exercised.
- `test/quote-reply.test.cjs`: new test checking the opt-out attribute, the font of paragraph, heading, list, bold and inline-code nodes under both font settings, and that bold keeps weight 700.

## Risks and rollback

Low. Only the quoted block in the dialog changes. Rollback: revert this PR.

## QA

- Exact base commit: 507aaadf9f0a6f4b65c8d4b1307ff73b683bc958 (`pre`)
- Exact candidate commit: 0adfcb3320448ba7aaba484d0db85362ba5d1d7d
- Before: computed font of the bold span in the dialog was the system stack; in the conversation it was the embedded font.
- After: covered by the new unit test; CI job "Install, typecheck, and test" passed on the candidate commit.
- Screenshots or video, if relevant: NOT RUN. The issue asks for computed-style readings and one capture on an isolated Paseo 0.15.0 host.
- Gaps or limitations: no real-host reading yet.

fix(notifications): align chevron disclosure and expose expanded state

## Summary

Aligns the account/repository notification chevrons with standard disclosure conventions and exposes the expanded state to assistive technology.

- Closed sections use a right chevron; open sections use a down chevron.
- Empty sections follow the same rule instead of using a left (back/previous) chevron.
- Removed the no-records-specific tooltip; the toggle now always describes its action (`Show`/`Hide` notifications), matching populated sections.
- Simplified `getChevronDetails` to depend only on visibility.
- Added `aria-expanded` to the account and repository toggles.

`aria-controls` is intentionally omitted because the notification list is flattened and virtualized, so there is no per-section panel element to reference.

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- `pnpm exec vp lint` and `vp fmt --check` on changed files
- Targeted Vitest suites for notification headers, list behavior, and display/icon helpers
- `pnpm i18n:check`

fix(schema): say the serial argument's enum offers the system names only

Follow-up to #23's auto-review nit: with the system labels listed, every `serial` argument published an enum of names while its description promised "its name as listed here, or its serial number", so a schema-validating client would refuse the serial the description offered.

Neither suggested fix is taken, on purpose:

- **Serials in the enum** would make a host that fans a question out over the enum's values (mcp-host context groups, `subjectLabels` in `intent-tools.ts`) read every system twice, once by name and once by serial.
- **`examples` instead of `enum`** would stop that fan-out entirely: the gateway reads `enum` only (spec D5), so iaqualink would answer every group question with a `no-subjects` line.

So the contract is the names, and the description now says so, noting that the server still resolves a serial for a caller that does not validate against the schema (`resolveSerial`, unchanged). The module comment records why the serials stay out of the enum, and a test guards that the enum lists each system once, by name.

Verified: `npm run test:coverage` — 328 tests, typecheck clean, 100% on every axis.

Closes #24

fix(hermes-cc): say which exit code a failed shell step returned instead of a generic message

## Linked issue

Refs #168

## Type of change

Fix: a failed shell step with a structured non-zero exit code now says which code it returned.

## Reasoning

For a shell step that ran and exited non-zero, step details showed an Error line reading "Tool call failed", although the command did run and its exit code is in the output.

## Goals

- When the step is a shell call, the provider reported a structured non-zero `exitCode`, and no error object was supplied, show `Command exited with code N` (en, zh-CN, ja).
- Keep the rule that an error description is never derived from output text.

## Non-goals

- Zero or missing exit codes, non-shell tools, and steps that carry a real error object keep today's message.
- How exit codes are read.

## Changes

- `server/hermes-cc/acp-tool-compat.ts`: the generic fallback error carries the integer non-zero shell exit code when one was reported.
- `client/tool-error.ts` and the three locale files: render the localized message from that code.
- Tests: `test/hermes-cc-acp-tools.test.cjs`, `test/translations.test.cjs` (messages in all three locales, copy error, and the negative cases).

## Risks and rollback

Low. Only the fallback sentence for failed shell steps changes. Rollback: revert this PR.

## QA

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: read files and render PDF pages off the main thread

## Problem
Tauri v2 runs non-async commands on the main thread, so a long command freezes the window while it runs. After #100 moved the app and folder list and icon commands off the main thread, three read-only commands were still synchronous:

- `read_file_bytes`: used by the PDF and code previews, and called once per file by indexing
- `render_pdf_page_native`: draws a PDF page with CoreGraphics
- `load_runtime_index`: loads the whole search data at startup and on refresh

## Fix
- All three are now `async` and do their work in `spawn_blocking`. The command results are unchanged, so the frontend needs no changes.
- They only read:
  - Concurrent calls are safe.
  - The runtime index is saved with an atomic rename, so a concurrent read never sees a half-written file.
  - CoreGraphics can be used off the main thread.
- Commands that change state (`sync_index_manifest`, `reset_index`, `save_search_feedback`, …) stay on the main thread, which keeps them in order without locks. Window and tray commands stay too, because AppKit requires the main thread.
- This also clears the long-standing clippy `needless_return` warning in `files.rs`.
- Docs: system-architecture 2.2 (2.9.1) and the docs index (2.6.1).

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` (no warnings), `cargo test`
- [x] `npm run test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`
- [x] Checked in the app: PDF and code previews, and searching right after launch

Fix activation of extensions with an underscore in their plugin ID

## References

Fixes #20380

## Code changes

`DefaultSchemaValidator` hands the plugin ID to Ajv as the schema ID. Ajv validates schema IDs as URIs through `fast-uri`, and a scheme may only contain letters, digits, `+`, `-` and `.`. A plugin ID such as `my_extension:plugin` therefore throws `TypeError: URI scheme is malformed.` and the extension never activates.

The schemas are now registered under `jupyterlab-plugin:<encoded plugin ID>` instead of the bare ID, so any plugin ID maps to a valid schema key. `_load()` also re-throws non-array failures instead of iterating over them, so the real error is reported rather than a `errors.forEach is not a function` `TypeError`.

## User-facing changes

Extensions whose plugin ID contains a character that is not valid in a URI scheme (for example an underscore) activate again ~~on 4.6.5 and later~~ after failing in 4.6.5 and 4.7.0b0.

> **Added by a maintainer**
>
> - `my_extension:plugin` fails in 4.6.5, while a scoped ID such as `@scope/my_extension:plugin` does not.
> - The newest wheels of 55 extensions on PyPI that are built for JupyterLab 4 have an unscoped ID with an underscore, among them `jupyterlab_code_formatter:settings`.

## Backwards-incompatible changes

None. The schema keys are internal to the validator and are not exposed through `ISettingRegistry`.

## AI usage

- Was AI used to generate this change? Yes.
- Was the generated change reviewed and run by a human before opening this PR? Yes — the new tests were run against the patched and the unpatched source, failing on the latter.
- Which AI tool and model were used? DeepSeek Harness with deepseek-v4.1-flash; Opus 5.5 (max effort) for the maintainer changes.

## Testing

```
cd packages/settingregistry && jlpm test
```

Three tests are added to `test/settingregistry.spec.ts`:

- `should accept a plugin ID that is not a valid schema URI` (validator level)
- `should load a plugin whose ID is not a valid schema URI` (registry level)
- `should reject with the validator error if a schema fails to register`

Against the unpatched source they fail with `TypeError: URI scheme is malformed.`, `TypeError: errors.forEach is not a function`, and the masked error respectively.
